_comment: Expected PB-007 fill for examples/case.example.json. This case exercises the appointment_level=limited path. NOTE: only fields gated to that path (or unconditional fields) get a value; the standard_* and expanded_* fields MUST be null because their writable_when conditions evaluate to false.

_writable_when_branching.appointment_level=standard: writes: standard_other_provisions (NOT written here — gated to standard)
_writable_when_branching.appointment_level=expanded: writes: expanded_duties + 30+ expanded_* sub-fields (NOT written here)

fields.case_title: In re Guardianship of A.M.R. (a Minor)
fields.good_cause_findings: Petition and opposition raise disputed material facts about the minor's primary caretaker and the father's involvement. Court finds it necessary under 18-C § 1-115 to appoint a GAL to investigate.
fields.fee_factors: Cap of 20 hours reasonable for the limited scope; party responsibility split 50/50 between petitioner and father.
fields.limited_duties: Interview the minor, the petitioner (maternal grandmother), and the father (Marcus Hill). Review the minor's school records. Submit a written report to the court within 30 days.
fields.limited_hearing_appearance: Appear at the contested hearing on 2026-06-08 if the report does not resolve the disputed issues.

_validator_expectations.writable_when on standard_*/expanded_* f: all null → no `not_writable` violations (these fields are gated and stay blank)
_validator_expectations.what would fail: if the LLM populated any expanded_* or standard_* field while appointment_level='limited', validator would flag `not_writable` for each one — this is exactly the writability-cascade catch the form needs
